transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. AI. What brings you in today?
I've been seeing and hearing things that aren't actually there, and it's starting to really overwhelm me. I just need help making these voices and images stop.
Have you also had any major mood episodes, like feeling unusually high or energized for days at a time, or feeling very depressed for weeks at a time, around the same period as the voices and images?

Yes, I've had periods where I felt extremely high, energized, and hyperactive, like I was on top of the world. A lot of the time, those high-energy phases overlapped with when I was hearing and seeing things, but I've also had the hallucinations during times when my mood was completely normal.
When the hallucinations happened while your mood was completely normal, did they last for at least 2 weeks without any major mood symptoms?

Yes, definitely. There was a period of about two or three weeks where I was still hearing voices and seeing things, but my mood was completely flat and normal. I didn't have any of that high energy or excitement at all during those weeks.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks where you felt very depressed or lost interest in things, while the hallucinations or other psychotic symptoms were still happening?

No, I haven't ever felt depressed or lost interest in things like that. My mood struggles have actually been the complete opposite, where I feel extremely energetic, high, or sometimes really easily irritated.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Schizophrenia, Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)], but the patient now reports clear manic episodes and also a period of 2–3 weeks of hallucinations with completely normal mood. That pattern supports schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type, because psychotic symptoms occur both during mood episodes and for at least 2 weeks outside mood episodes. Schizophrenia is less likely because prominent mood episodes are present.

The report of hallucinations occurring during euthymic periods makes pure mood-congruent psychosis less likely, so Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features is no longer supported. Delusional Disorder is also less likely because the patient has prominent hallucinations, not just delusions. Depressive-type schizoaffective disorder is not supported because the described mood episodes are elevated rather than depressive. The remaining differential is schizophrenia vs schizoaffective disorder (bipolar type) vs bipolar I disorder with psychotic features, depending on whether psychosis has occurred for at least 2 weeks without mood symptoms and whether mood episodes occupy a substantial portion of the illness.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has clear psychotic symptoms (auditory and visual hallucinations) plus recurrent manic-spectrum episodes with elevated/energized, hyperactive, and irritable mood. Crucially, there was a documented 2–3 week period of hallucinations occurring while mood was completely normal, which supports schizoaffective disorder rather than bipolar disorder with psychotic features. There is no history of a major depressive episode.
